If sentiment is positive (≥0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract bearish bias.

If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 1–2% for late horizon (16–30 days) to prevent overcorrection.

If sentiment is positive but forecast is trending downward, reverse the direction by +0.5–1.0% for mid horizon to align with sentiment momentum.

If sentiment is negative and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 1–2% for early horizon to avoid false bullish signals.

If sentiment is neutral and forecast is flat, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for late horizon to capture latent bullish sentiment.
